qualification: Intel host-backed preboot block read through the canonical driver and virtualizer
observations: Root mapped the PCI register pages uncached into virtio_blk, and the coherent DMA frame into virtio_blk and blk_virt. The VMM retained only its own block queue page.
Before continuing firmware execution, the VMM submitted a 4096-byte read through its queue, required host-backed attachment and compared every returned byte against the test prefix and zero padding.
Root reported x86 host block queue read verified; the Intel run also passed Linux ring3 initramfs syscalls and the bidirectional console exchange.
The full Spark gate includes ASan/UBSan boot-read tests with the canonical queue pump: block offset, bounds, error response without output modification, and refusal after guest DRIVER_OK.

The initial Intel attempt refused startup because capability order allocated a later physical page first. Ascending, deduplicated frame allocation fixed that failure; the retained successful run uses the corrected revision.
limitations: This is preboot VMM media staging, not a block request submitted by the Linux guest. Guest block enumeration remains incomplete.
The 32 MiB medium is a fresh read-only qualification fixture. Pinned Debian and writable flush/reboot persistence are not qualified.
Intel denial probes, multi-client isolation and resource reclamation were not exercised by this run.
PCI reset timeout and mapping-failure injection were not exercised.
Canonical integration, GUI qualification and the v0.4 release remain incomplete.
